sense.text:
One of the most important scriptures in the Bible, because it answers the question of life: what is the point of life, what is our purpose? “Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.”

Everything else is vanity. All the tangible things we have, we could lose in one minute, and when we go to the grave we take nothing with us. Only our good works or our bad works follow us into the grave.

“For God shall bring every work into judgment”: every single work, small or great. We do not want to stand on the opposite side of that judgment with nothing but bad works.

“With every secret thing”: whatever we think we have done in secret. The word secret is written here, but there is no secret thing unto the Most High God, whose eyes are ten thousand times brighter than the sun. That is for anyone still in the midst of adultery, fornication, pornography, malice, envy and hatred: God will bring every secret thing into judgment, “whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” We do not want our evil works brought forth before the Most High; we want the Most High to blot them out.

Christ is our tabernacle: that is the word this Sabbath, in preparation for the first night of the feast of tabernacles, also called the feast of booths, Sukkot.

“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.” If you want wisdom, you must fear God. The Most High will not reveal his mysteries to you, and your wisdom will not increase, while you live in continuous sin. None of our forefathers and none of the prophets was endowed with wisdom while being a wicked man. It is not in the Bible.

“A good understanding have all they that do his commandments”: those are action words. God is looking for the application, not for those who can parakeet scriptures, but for brothers and sisters willing to apply them. Those who took off work, or brought their work with them, to keep the feast are an example of that application. It may be uncomfortable, but it is done for the Most High and a greater purpose, because the whole duty of man is to keep God’s commandments. “His praise endureth for ever.”

precepts.why:
“He revealeth the deep and secret things”, but unto whom? Only unto his servants, only unto those who fear God and keep his commandments, because the fear of God is the beginning of wisdom.

“He knoweth what is in the darkness, and the light dwelleth with him.” We want the Most High to show us that light and keep bringing forth the beautiful meanings out of the Bible. For him to do so, we have to walk in wisdom as our forefather Daniel did.

Why did God reveal the deep and secret things unto Daniel? The children here are Daniel and his brethren: “Children in whom was no blemish”, no spiritual blemish or physical blemish, “but well favoured”. They knew how to carry themselves, not only with the Most High but in the midst of the other nations; they were well mannered.

“Skilful in all wisdom, and cunning in knowledge, and understanding science”: they were not dumb children; they were educated in every subject, “such as had ability in them to stand in the king’s palace”.

Read Daniel 2:22 again with that: he had no blemish, he was well favoured, he was skilful in wisdom, he had discernment, and more importantly he was applying the laws of God. That is why the deep and secret things were revealed to him.

“Surely the Lord God will do nothing, but he revealeth his secret unto his servants the prophets.”

One secret was that we are the Israelites. Some of us found that out in the 80s, the 90s and the early 2000s. It was kept from us: when our forefathers got off the first documented slave ship at Jamestown, Virginia, the royal house of David, many of them did not know they were Israelites. That understanding was destroyed from them and taken from them.

Another secret is Leviticus 23, our high holy days. In the world we celebrated Christmas, Thanksgiving, birthdays and Easter, ungodly things taught to us by our oppressors, and thought the feasts were for the so-called white man in Israel posing as a Jew. The Most High said no, those are your high holy days, and he revealed them by sending the prophets before us, the bishops, who gave us the knowledge we have now. And the prophets are only the Israelites.

“And I raised up of your sons for prophets, and of your young men for Nazarites.” Out of your sons come the prophets: the sons of Judah, Benjamin, Levi, Ephraim, the whole twelve tribes, and nobody else. “Is it not even thus, O ye children of Israel?”

If your sons are the true prophets, the opposite of truth is false: the nations are false prophets. Everything we learned came from false prophets, even our kindred brothers in the world who are pastors and ministers, because they teach the doctrine of the other nations, and all the religions that were forced upon us.

sense.text:
Christ is speaking to the disciples, the elect: “it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.” To them, the other Israelites, it is not given.

It is unto the elect to know the mysteries, and the elect is in Israel United in Christ. It goes further: the twelve are in IUIC. Let the other camps make their hate videos; the twelve disciples, the apostles, are back on this earth and in IUIC. We do not know who they are, but they are here.

Some of the mysteries shown to the servants in IUIC: the new moon, while the whole world keeps a false moon, either a dark moon or a little sliver of light; Passover being the Lord’s birth; and something as simple as one wife, which is hard for a negro and for brothers in the other camps to understand. That secret has been shown unto us.

There are a lot of mysteries in this Bible. “The mystery which hath been hid from ages and from generations”: that we are the Israelites; that Jesus Christ is a black man with woolly white hair who died only for the nation of Israel; that we are God’s chosen people; that the so-called Hispanics, natives and descendants of slaves, are part of the twelve tribes and our brothers as well. Christ died to bring both nations back to one.

“But now is made manifest to his saints.” Not everybody is a saint. The Catholic church makes saints, like Mother Teresa after reviewing her works, but they cannot be saints, the same way they cannot be Christians and cannot be Jews.
“To whom God would make known what is the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles”: among the scattered Israelites, “which is Christ in you, the hope of glory”.

precepts.why:
Who are the saints? “He also exalteth the horn of his people”: the horn of his people is Christ. “The praise of all his saints; even of the children of Israel”.

That word even means indeed; that is why it is in italics. Indeed the children of Israel. So the saints, to whom the mystery is made manifest, are only the children of Israel.

Paul speaks of “the revelation of the mystery, which was kept secret since the world began”: that the Gentiles would be grafted in, meaning the scattered Israelites.

“But now is made manifest, and by the scriptures of the prophets, according to the commandment of the everlasting God, made known to all nations for the obedience of faith”. Some will hear “all nations” and fall off the horse, but it says all nations because we were scattered into all nations, according to Deuteronomy 4:27. The mystery made known among the nations is the scattered Israelites being brought back. “To God only wise, be glory through Jesus Christ for ever. Amen.”

sense.text:
Who was Paul writing to in the book of Romans? Brothers hear the word Rome and fall off the horse, just like the Christian pastors.

“I could wish that myself were accursed from Christ”: Paul wished he could go through the same things Christ went through, “for my brethren”. Modern society teaches that everybody is one in Jesus, all brothers in Christ, the Arab man, the white man and the black man; yet the black man is always at the bottom. That is not what Paul is talking about. His brethren are “my kinsmen according to the flesh”, and that is how you get kinsmen: by sex.

“Who are Israelites”: that clarifies it, crystal clear. The twelve tribes of Israel. To them pertain “the adoption, and the glory, and the covenants”, covenants with an s: the Old Testament and the New Testament are only for the Israelites. “The giving of the law” was given to the priests, and now under Christ we are all priests of the Most High; “and the service of God, and the promises”.

“Of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came”: Christ came in the flesh through sex, the same way his brothers were made. There was no divine incarnation, also known today as the immaculate deception. There is no such thing in the Bible. “Who is over all, God blessed for ever. Amen.”

precepts.why:
Since Paul says “my kinsmen according to the flesh”, get some colour. Revelation 1:14 and the Song of Solomon are not the only colour scriptures: the whole Bible tells you what the Israelite, God’s chosen people, looks like. People are still beguiled by the false image of Jesus Christ, the white image of Cesare Borgia that is everywhere on this planet, which is witchcraft. In places like Ghana and Sierra Leone our people were perplexed to learn that Jesus Christ is a black man and that his description is written in the Bible.

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” Joseph was sold as a slave into Egypt, among other black people, and he blended in with them: their clothing, and their complexion. His own brothers did not recognise him.

“And they knew not that Joseph understood them; for he spake unto them by an interpreter.” If Joseph had been a white man among the Egyptians, his brothers would have said, this is Joseph. But he spoke with an interpreter, and they took him for one of the ancient Egyptians. He looked just like them.

That is crystal clear, as simple as two plus two. That is why we say Christianity is worse than crack: only a crackhead could miss it. It is that simple and basic to understand, but Christianity being the drug that it is, our people are confused.

Joseph went up to bury his father, and with him went “all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt”, together with “all the house of Joseph, and his brethren, and his father’s house”. The Egyptians and Jacob’s family went up together, and “there they mourned with a great and very sore lamentation”.

“And when the inhabitants of the land, the Canaanites”, the Africans, the pure-blooded Nilotes, “saw the mourning in the floor of Atad, they said, This is a grievous mourning to the Egyptians”. They mistook the Hebrews for Egyptians.

There are many more colour scriptures than Revelation 1:14 and the basics. This whole Bible is a sword, and the brothers have to know how to unsheath it and use it correctly. Nobody should be getting confounded.

Many names within our nation denote black appearance; Acts 13:2 is not the only one. “Eleazar Aaron’s son took him one of the daughters of Putiel to wife; and she bare him Phinehas”.

The scholars give the meaning of Phinehas: it comes from an Egyptian name, from the word the Egyptians used for their southern neighbours, which came to mean the black, or the Nubian; another work renders it the bronze-coloured one; and Brown-Driver-Briggs gives it plainly as the negro. That is not something we made up; the scholars know it while many of us do not.

Phinehas was Aaron’s grandson, so the Levites were black.

The word Cushi was racial terminology in the Hebrew Bible for a dark-skinned person of African descent, because Cush was one of the sons of Ham, and Ham was the progenitor of the dark races, the pure-blooded Nilotes. In the land of Israel today, when Amalek calls our Ethiopian brothers and sisters Cushi, it is a derogatory word, and you will never find a so-called rabbi named Rabbi Cush, because they know it means black.

But were the Israelites ever called Cush in the Bible? “Jehudi the son of Nethaniah, the son of Shelemiah, the son of Cushi”. Jehudi is another name for Jew, like Yehudi or Yehuda. This was an Israelite named Cushi: the son of black.
“The word of the Lord which came unto Zephaniah the son of Cushi”. Zephaniah is a prophet; we read his book. And he was the son of Cushi: his father was called black.

sense.text:
Now into the topic. “Lo, I come: in the volume of the book it is written of me”. Every nuance of this Bible, every single word and every single letter, deals with Christ. Christ is in the Old Testament as he is in the New. He comes in the volume of the book, from Genesis all the way to Revelation.

That is why he spoke with double meaning, and why you can read this Bible to heaven and back, four chapters every day, and never know enough. The Most High keeps showing mystery after mystery, and he is using the men of this house to do it; the Bishop is still bringing out fire classes every Sabbath. That is how you know you are in the right place.
“I delight to do thy will, O my God”: the will of God is to keep the commandments. “Yea, thy law is within my heart.”

precepts.why:
Go to the beginning of the volume of the book, to show a mystery of the Bible that only pertains to us, one Bishop Kani brought out. Adam had Cain and Abel; Abel was the righteous, the chosen, but Cain slew him, and Seth replaced him. We are going down the royal line, the chosen line that came out of Adam.

Adam means man (not red earth; stop listening to dumb Amalekites). “Called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel”. Seth means appointed. Most of the time the meaning of the name is right there in the verse.

Out of Seth came Enos: “he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Enos means mortal.

Keep going down the line. “Enos lived ninety years, and begat Cainan”: Cainan means sorrow. So far: man, appointed, mortal, sorrow.

“Cainan lived seventy years, and begat Mahalaleel”: Mahalaleel means praise of God, or blessed God. “Mahalaleel lived sixty and five years, and begat Jared”: Jared means shall come down, or descend. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch”: Enoch means trained in righteousness (some have it as dedicated); “Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for God took him.”

“Enoch lived sixty and five years, and begat Methuselah”: Methuselah means when he dies, it shall come. “Methuselah lived an hundred eighty and seven years, and begat Lamech”: Lamech means despair, or sorrow. And Lamech “called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands”: Noah means comfort, or rest.

Put the names together and they read: man appointed mortal sorrow; the blessed God shall come down, trained in righteousness; when he dies it shall come; sorrow, then comfort. That is Christ, written in the line of the fathers. When Christ said, Lo, I come in the volume of the book, he meant it.

“That he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is!” The secrets of wisdom are double. We take things at face value, but there are deeper meanings.

To get that deeper meaning you must be keeping the commandments, as Psalms 111:10 says. That is the only way wisdom and understanding will grow; there is no other way on this earth.

The names in our record book, our constitution: did we just make them up? Absolutely not. The book of Genesis in Hebrew is Bereshith, which means in the beginning, and the word is right there in verse one: “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” The first verse tells you what the book is about.
Exodus means to exit or come out, but in Hebrew the book is Shemot, which means names. And verse one says it: “Now these are the names of the children of Israel, which came into Egypt”.
Leviticus in Hebrew is Vayikra, meaning and he called. Right there in the first verse: “And the Lord called unto Moses”.

Numbers in Hebrew is Bamidbar, which means in the wilderness: “And the Lord spake unto Moses in the wilderness of Sinai”. Now you see where the meanings of these names came from. The Most High is a genius, and he gave those secrets unto us.

Deuteronomy in Hebrew is Devarim, which means words, or things spoken: “These be the words which Moses spake unto all Israel”. These be the devarim, spoken unto all Israel: only Israelites, nobody else.

sense.text: Now to the Most High’s holy day, because the word is Christ our tabernacle, in preparation for the feast of tabernacles, which begins tomorrow night at even. The feasts, with an s, are “holy convocations”: “even these are my feasts”, indeed, these are my feasts.
“Six days shall work be done: but the seventh day is the sabbath of rest”: this goes into the Sabbath, “the sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.”
“These are the feasts of the Lord, even holy convocations”: holy gatherings, which is what we are doing now. “Which ye shall proclaim in their seasons”: these high holy days are seasonal.

“The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days unto the Lord”: the feast of tabernacles, also known as the feast of booths, Sukkot. “On the first day shall be an holy convocation: ye shall do no servile work therein”: no working from Sunday night to Monday night, if you can.
“Seven days ye shall offer an offering made by fire unto the Lord”. We do not offer fire offerings any more, because Christ replaced that: the same man who said, Lo, I come in the volume of the book.

“A burnt offering, and a meat offering, a sacrifice, and drink offerings, every thing upon his day”. We had to bring forth those offerings. Our offerings today are repentance, keeping the commandments and righteousness.

The seventh month is the month we are in now, by God’s standards. The Most High names the trees used to reverence the feast of tabernacles, “the boughs of goodly trees, branches of palm trees, and the boughs of thick trees, and willows of the brook”: this is how we made our booths.

“Ye shall rejoice before the Lord your God seven days.” The Most High does not want to see frowns. Many are going through different things, but now is not the time to sorrow; it is time to rejoice in the Lord.

“It shall be a statute for ever in your generations”: our sons and daughters were supposed to keep this forever. But we fell off. Sin came into the picture, the Most High put his big black foot in our behind, and we forgot who we are: our customs, our heritage, everything.

“All that are Israelites born shall dwell in booths”: not Moabite born, not Edomite born, Israelites born. What do the nations have to do with God? Not a damn thing. The Most High’s statutes and judgments were given to Israel alone.

“That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths”. Everything we do is to reverence the Most High; everything is about Christ. Our whole life has to be dedicated to the Most High, because with a snap of a finger he can take it away.

Almost every other verse ends with “I am the Lord your God.” He keeps telling us because we were given to idolatry: over four hundred years in Egypt worshipping frogs, crocodiles, lice and all sorts of gods, and the same in America. When Christ brings us out of here he will say it all over again: I am the Lord your God. Get Christmas out of your head; get the white man out of your mind. We are a hard-headed people.

“And Moses declared unto the children of Israel the feasts of the Lord.” The same way we are declaring the feast of the Lord to our brothers and sisters again, especially those who are new and watching online: read about it, and keep it to the best of your ability.

precepts.why:
Why does it say “every thing upon his day”? “When any will offer a meat offering unto the Lord, his offering shall be of fine flour; and he shall pour oil upon it, and put frankincense thereon: And he shall bring it to Aaron’s sons the priests”.

The people had to bring their offerings to the priests. The priests and the high priests were not the only ones doing the work; every man had work to do, each bringing his offering upon his day.

The Most High gave us these statutes and our high holy days, and we forgot them, because he removed them from us; he had the white man beat them out of us. Baruch prays, “As thou spakest by thy servant Moses”: “If ye will not hear my voice, surely this very great multitude shall be turned into a small number among the nations, where I will scatter them.” You read about that in Deuteronomy 28:15-68.

“For I knew that they would not hear me, because it is a stiffnecked people”. That is us, the so-called blacks and Hispanics. Turn on the TV, or watch the brothers at camp telling our people how great they are: go to Kenya, read Deuteronomy 7:6, and get hit with a stone, for telling people they are above all nations and that the Messiah looks like them and died for them.

“But in the land of their captivities they shall remember themselves”: in America, Jamaica, wherever we are on this earth. We are going to remember the Sabbaths and the feast of tabernacles. “I will give them an heart, and ears to hear”, and that is what the Most High is doing now. “And return from their stiff neck, and from their wicked deeds”.

There is a remnant that will return to him. His word never comes back void, and brothers and sisters will repent. So our job is to go onto the highways and byways and compel them to come in, even if it is one person. We are not doing this in vain: teach his words, not your own, and he will bring them in. “I will no more drive my people of Israel out of the land that I have given them.”

sense.text:
In chapter 7 the walls and doors of Jerusalem were rebuilt, and there was a registry of the names of those who came back from the captivity of Babylon. Right before the feast of tabernacles every family had to register. It is the same now: to attend the feast of tabernacles, here and everywhere it is kept, you register at the front. We are rehearsing the righteous acts, doing the same thing all over again, though we are still in captivity.

“All the people gathered themselves together as one man”, and asked Ezra “to bring the book of the law of Moses, which the Lord had commanded to Israel.”
“Upon the first day of the seventh month”: this is the memorial of blowing of trumpets.
“The ears of all the people were attentive unto the book of the law.” They were not on their phones; they were not talking. They were paying attention.
“Ezra the scribe stood upon a pulpit of wood”, with men standing beside him on his right hand and his left: Ezra had his camp going on.
“So they read in the book in the law of God distinctly, and gave the sense, and caused them to understand the reading.” They gave the discernment distinctly.

To find what was written, they were reading the word of the Lord distinctly, searching and reasoning. “They found written in the law which the Lord had commanded by Moses, that the children of Israel should dwell in booths in the feast of the seventh month”. There is a reason that word dwell is stressed.

They made booths, as it is written, “every one upon the roof of his house, and in their courts”, and sat under them, “for since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun unto that day had not the children of Israel done so.” For a very long time they had not kept the feast of tabernacles.

It was the same for us when we got off those cargo slave ships. But now the comforter, the spirit of Christ, has returned that understanding to us, and we understand that we must keep the feast of tabernacles.
“In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.” Some Israelites cannot even understand that. “The same was in the beginning with God”: that is Christ.

“And the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us”. The Greek word for dwelt is skenoo: to dwell, to tabernacle, to pitch a tent. The Word was made flesh and tabernacled among us, pitched his tent among us, when Christ walked the earth.

“And we beheld his glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father”: the same glory that filled the tabernacle.

Christ our Lord and Saviour is the living presence of the Father among Israel, just as the tabernacle represented God’s presence among Israel in old times. Christ is our tabernacle.

precepts.why:
“But Christ being come an high priest of good things to come, by a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with hands”. He himself was the tabernacle, and he also went into the tabernacle in the heavens, because the tabernacle on earth was made after the image of the one in heaven.

“Neither by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered in once into the holy place, having obtained eternal redemption for us.” Christ only had to do it once: he only had to die once. In the old tabernacle Aaron and his sons had to enter the holy of holies once a year to atone for us. Christ, the walking embodiment of the tabernacle, did it once.

“Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

All the offerings we had to bring on the feast of tabernacles were a shadow of things to come, because Christ replaced them: the drink offerings, the meat offerings, the sacrifices. That unblemished lamb we had to offer, Christ replaced; the body is of Christ.

What was in the tabernacle? “Then a cloud covered the tent of the congregation, and the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle.” The main tabernacle stood in the middle, with Israel pitching their tents on the outskirts. Inside was the ark of the covenant, and the glory from the majesty of the Most High, the light shining forth in the holy of holies.

“And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of the congregation, because the cloud abode thereon”. Now go back to John 1:14: the word dwelt means to pitch a tent, to tabernacle, and “we beheld his glory”: that same glory that filled the tabernacle in Exodus 40.

“For in him dwelleth all the fulness of the Godhead bodily.” The him is Christ. “And ye are complete in him, which is the head of all principality and power”.

All that glory, all that glorious manifestation we read about, is Christ. Christ is Yahawah. Christ was the father that we dealt with: not the main Father, but the father we dealt with, and he is our father because we come from him.

sense.text: “The first covenant had also ordinances of divine service”, divine service by the priests and high priests, “and a worldly sanctuary”, worldly because it was on earth.

“The first, wherein was the candlestick”, the menorah, on the left side of the tabernacle, “and the table, and the shewbread” on the right side. Everything was made of real gold. “Which is called the sanctuary.”

“And after the second veil, the tabernacle which is called the Holiest of all”. With the veil drawn open you see the ark of the covenant. “The golden censer”: the incense that went up like prayers to the Most High. “The cherubims of glory shadowing the mercyseat” sit on the ark with their wings touching, and the glory of God in the centre. “Of which we cannot now speak particularly”: Paul wanted to get heavy with them on that.

“The priests went always into the first tabernacle, accomplishing the service of God. But into the second went the high priest alone once every year”. The regular priests of the Levitical line could not go into the second tabernacle; only the high priest, Aaron and his sons, the high priests’ lineage. Christ did it once in the heavens when he died for us; on earth the high priest had to do it once every year.

“For Christ is not entered into the holy places made with hands”, the tabernacle pictured on the screen, “which are the figures of the true”, symbolic of the true things in heaven, “but into heaven itself, now to appear in the presence of God for us”.

The mercy seat with the glory of God at its centre represents Christ: imagine Christ sitting on the throne, with two huge angels stretching out their wings. He is now the new high priest, the mediator who walks into the holy of holies in the heavens on our behalf.

“As the high priest entereth into the holy place every year with blood of others”: they went into the holy of holies once a year, but Christ only had to do it once. “But now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.”

“So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many”, many of the Israelites. “And unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.” That is exactly what we are waiting for.

precepts.why:
The figures of the true were made by pattern. They “serve unto the example and shadow of heavenly things, as Moses was admonished of God when he was about to make the tabernacle: for, See, saith he, that thou make all things according to the pattern shewed to thee in the mount.”

What Moses made was a shadow of the things in the heavens. What was shown him in the mount were the things in heaven; they had to be made with earthly hands, but all of it was symbolic of what is really above us. That is why Christ entered not the holy places made with hands but heaven itself.

sense.text: “Thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold”, with “six branches” coming out of its sides, three on one side and three on the other: that is the menorah.

“And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof”: seven lamps. Not ten, not nine, not eight; stop following Amalek. “That they may give light over against it.” That light was used inside the tabernacle. Christ, in his presence and his glory, replaced it: he is the light we have to follow.

precepts.why: “I am the light of the world”: the Israelite world. “He that followeth me shall not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.” The light of the lamps in the tabernacle was Christ. Christ is our tabernacle.

Still explaining the light in the tabernacle: even the menorah was only a representation of Christ. “There will I make the horn of David to bud”, just as Aaron’s rod budded. “I have ordained a lamp for mine anointed.” The horn of David is Christ; he is the anointed, and he is that light.
“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. All of it is a representation of Jesus Christ.

Christ is that light that was in the tabernacle by way of the menorah. “Being turned, I saw seven golden candlesticks; And in the midst of the seven candlesticks one like unto the Son of man”: Christ, in the middle of the light, illuminating more than the lamps.

“His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow”: woolly textured hair, all white. “His eyes were as a flame of fire”: he drank wine, turned water into wine, and the Pharisees called him a winebibber. “His feet like unto fine brass, as if they burned in a furnace”: brown; that is how you refine brass, you burn it. He was black, blacky black. “His voice as the sound of many waters”, like thunder.

The point is the candlesticks: Christ was the same illumination we saw in the tabernacle. The glory over the mercy seat, the menorah, all of it was a representation of Christ.

“The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches”: the messengers, the leaders of the seven churches, “and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.” All a representation of Jesus Christ; the whole Bible is. Lo, I come in the volume of the book.

Remember, he sends forth his messenger to prepare his way. We are the messengers of God, all of us, the prophets: the ambassadors of Christ, laying forth the way and preparing this whole world for the entrance of Jesus Christ.

sense.text: The shewbread, the bread of presence. “Bake twelve cakes thereof”: twelve cakes representing the twelve tribes of Israel, set “in two rows, six on a row, upon the pure table before the Lord.”

“Every sabbath he shall set it in order before the Lord continually, being taken from the children of Israel by an everlasting covenant.” Aaron and his sons “shall eat it in the holy place: for it is most holy unto him”: that is the holy of holies shown in the picture of the tabernacle.

precepts.why:
Christ was also that bread. “What sign shewest thou then, that we may see, and believe thee?” That was the wicked Pharisees and scribes: they always wanted a sign; his words were not enough. “Our fathers did eat manna in the desert”.

“Moses gave you not that bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread from heaven. For the bread of God is he which cometh down from heaven, and giveth life unto the world.” Forget the shewbread in the tabernacle and the bread of the offerings: the true bread was Jesus Christ, and the Pharisees were blinded to it.

They were raised in the law but hated Christ, because they wanted that seat and did not want Rome to take it. The pastors today are the same: they know we are the Israelites, they cannot be so stupid as not to understand Deuteronomy 28 and Revelation 1:14, but they want to keep their position in society and keep kissing Amalek’s behind. That is why they reject this Bible, and Christ will reject them when he comes back.

“Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king”. Where was Jesus born? Bethlehem. In Arabic the name is Beit Lahm, literally house of meat, and in Hebrew Beit Lechem, literally house of bread.

Christ was born in the house of bread because he is that true bread to come out of Bethlehem. He replaced the shewbread in the tabernacle. That is why he said, eat of my flesh. Surely a doctor of the law would have understood what he meant, but the Pharisees could not, and those who knew it rejected it openly to keep their position.

The prophecy. The New Testament was not yet written, so surely a doctor of the law had read Micah: “But thou, Beth–lehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel”. That is Christ, “whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.”

They knew the Messiah would be born out of Bethlehem, the house of bread, to become the new living bread. They knew it, and they rejected it, just like the pastors today.

“If we let him thus alone, all men will believe on him: and the Romans shall come and take away both our place and nation.” That is what they were worried about.

Caiaphas was “the high priest that same year”, well educated in the Tanakh, and said “that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” “He prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only, but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” The Gentiles scattered abroad are the children of God, the Israelites.

“Then from that day forth they took counsel together for to put him to death.” Wicked as hell. They rejected Micah and the prophecies; they knew Jesus Christ was the Saviour and still went after him and put him to death. But it was prophecy, and prophecy had to be fulfilled.

Those same pastors who reject Christ are back today, and this is their punishment. “But the fearful”: fearful to keep God’s commandments because of what Esau will say, afraid he will take away your place in society if you profess yourself an Israelite. “And unbelieving”: an unbelieving spirit that knows the commandments and rejects them; the Bible tells you Christ is black and you reject that.

“All liars, shall have their part in the lake which burneth with fire and brimstone”.

sense.text:
Christ, the walking embodiment of the tabernacle, the glory that was in the tabernacle and dwelt among us while we dwelt in the wilderness, also kept the feast of tabernacles when he was in the flesh: “Now the Jews’ feast of tabernacles was at hand.”

Our people in Christianity say the commandments are done away with, yet you have Christ keeping Dedication, keeping Passover, keeping tabernacles. What is wrong with you? You want to follow Esau; the white man has become your god.

“There was much murmuring among the people concerning him”: there was division in Israel, because some believed on Christ and some did not. Some said “He is a good man: others said, Nay; but he deceiveth the people.”

“About the midst of the feast Jesus went up into the temple, and taught.” He taught on the feast of tabernacles. The Jews marvelled: how does he know the law, and he did not go to any of our schools, “having never learned?”

“My doctrine is not mine, but his that sent me.” His doctrine is from the Father, the same way our doctrine should be from our Father. When we go out onto the highways and byways, the Most High did not send us to speak our own words. We have to speak the words that are in this Bible: Christ’s words.
“Will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles, and teach the Gentiles?” Into the scattered: teach the Israelites.

“In the last day, that great day of the feast”: the eighth day. It is called the great day because this feast was one of the three we were commanded to go up to Jerusalem to keep: Passover, the feast of firstfruits (also called Pentecost), and the feast of tabernacles.

Why would Christ cry “If any man thirst, let him come unto me, and drink” on the last day of the feast? Because of what was commanded on the feast in Leviticus 23: sacrifices, offerings, water libations, drink offerings, meat offerings.

“Out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.” When Christ said, drink of me, and spoke of living waters, he was replacing the water libations and the drink offerings by spilling his blood for the nation of Israel.

precepts.why: The meat offerings were flour “mingled with oil” for a bullock, a ram and a lamb, “a sacrifice made by fire unto the Lord.” Then the point: “And their drink offerings shall be half an hin of wine unto a bullock, and the third part of an hin unto a ram, and a fourth part of an hin unto a lamb”. We had to offer drink offerings, and Christ, crying come unto me and drink, replaced them.

“How he made a pool, and a conduit, and brought water into the city”. King Hezekiah made the pool, the pool of Siloam spoken of in John, around 700 BC. He used it to defend Jerusalem against the siege, and the pool was also used for ritual cleansing, especially during the feast.

“As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.” Christ made clay of the spittle, anointed the eyes of the blind man, “And said unto him, Go, wash in the pool of Siloam, (which is by interpretation, Sent.) He went his way therefore, and washed, and came seeing.”

Christ blessed this man by the pool Hezekiah made, from which many of our ritual cleansings came. Christ replaced all of that: all the diverse washings and baptisms.

sense.text: Still Christ being that tabernacle: everything done in the tabernacle was a shadow of things to come in Christ, a representation of Christ. “Two lambs of the first year day by day continually”: one lamb offered in the morning and the other at even.
“And the fourth part of an hin of wine for a drink offering.” We offered wine as drink offerings as well.
The evening lamb was offered “according to the meat offering of the morning, and according to the drink offering thereof”: an offering in the morning and an offering at even.

precepts.why: What are we talking about? The drink offerings. “He burnt his burnt offering and his meat offering, and poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings, upon the altar.” The drink offering was poured upon the altar.

Christ replaced all of that. “He took the cup, and gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it; For this is my blood of the new testament, which is shed for many for the remission of sins.” Christ’s blood replaced the drink offerings we poured on the altar.

sense.text: The washings the priests had to do. “A laver of brass”, “to wash withal”, set “between the tabernacle of the congregation and the altar”. The priest had to be clean: Aaron and his sons washed their hands and their feet when they went into the tabernacle or came near the altar to minister, “that they die not”, “a statute for ever to them”. In the old times a priest washed before serving, as a symbol of purification.

precepts.why:
Christ is that water. Now we are purified with the water of Christ, which is the word: “That he might sanctify and cleanse it with the washing of water by the word”.

This is what the Pharisees stumbled on: they could not understand that Christ replaced all those things; they were a shadow of things to come. “That he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing; but that it should be holy and without blemish.”

sense.text: The incense, the censer seen in the picture of the tabernacle. The altar of incense was put “before the vail that is by the ark of the testimony, before the mercy seat that is over the testimony, where I will meet with thee.”
“Aaron shall burn thereon sweet incense every morning: when he dresseth the lamps, he shall burn incense upon it.” And at even, “a perpetual incense before the Lord throughout your generations.”

precepts.why: “Let my prayer be set forth before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.” When Aaron burned the incense, he was sending up prayers on our behalf; the incense is prayer.

But now under Christ: “It is Christ that died, yea rather, that is risen again, who is even at the right hand of God, who also maketh intercession for us.”

Christ is sitting at the right hand of the Father, the mediator making intercession for us. Before, it was Aaron sending up the prayers with the censer and the incense; now we have Christ at the right hand of the Father making intercession for the Israelites.

sense.text: “They that are delivered from the noise of archers in the places of drawing water, there shall they rehearse the righteous acts of the Lord”. We are rehearsing the righteous acts of the Lord in the places of drawing water, in Babylon the great, where we were brought as slaves. Wherever there is an IUIC congregation, they will celebrate the feast of tabernacles: rehearsing the righteous acts of our forefathers, “the righteous acts toward the inhabitants of his villages in Israel”.

precepts.why:
“Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.” We are the future judges of the earth. We rehearse the righteous acts because when the Most High comes back and puts that crown on your head, you men will judge this planet earth; that is why he is called the King of kings.

“Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice with trembling. Kiss the Son”. “Blessed are all they that put their trust in him.”

“Love righteousness, ye that be judges of the earth”. Here we are rehearsing the righteous acts, keeping the Sabbaths, keeping the feast of the Lord: love righteousness, you judges of the earth, and seek the Lord, “in simplicity of heart seek him.”

sense.text: We read in John 1:14 that the Word was made flesh and dwelt among us: he pitched his tent among men. Christ was that tabernacle. “And there was no more sea”: that is the rulership; no more nations.

“Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men”. Who is that tabernacle? Christ. “And he will dwell with them”: he will pitch his tent with us, “and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God.” And they say Christ is not our God.

“And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes”: God here is Christ. “And there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away.”

“I am Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the end”, just as he said in Revelation 1: the first and the last. “I will give unto him that is athirst of the fountain of the water of life freely”: the same thing he said in John 7:38, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.

“He that overcometh shall inherit all things; and I will be his God, and he shall be my son.” To get to this point we have to rehearse the righteous acts. When Christ comes back he will give us the power to subdue the nations.

The same way we keep the feast of tabernacles, this whole planet earth has to keep it: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

But we need power for that. We cannot do it with these weak bodies; we have no military and no might. We have to rehearse the righteous acts to be found worthy of that power.

Whoever will not come up, “even upon them shall be no rain.” If the family of Egypt, the pure-blooded Nilotic Hamites, will not come up to worship the Lord, “there shall be the plague, wherewith the Lord will smite the heathen that come not up to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

“And in that day there shall be no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts.” There will be no heathens in the land, no foreign nations; those dusty bastards over there are getting out of the land. Just Israelites, twelve tribes. That is a beautiful thing.

Rehearse the righteous acts: the time is now, the spiritual aspect of the war. “But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you”: the same with America. America is not listening; they see the videos, the marches and the blitzes, and they know we are the Israelites.

“That I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel”. God called the Israelites his armies before he brought them out. We are the armies of God, his military on earth, and that soldier mentality, being a soldier of the Lord, should be in each one of us on a spiritual level.

precepts.why:
An army has discipline: you discipline yourself to keep the commandments of God and are not easily shaken. “Thou therefore endure hardness, as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.” Not easily moved, not easily separated: no trial or tribulation on this earth is supposed to separate us from the love of Christ.

“No man that warreth entangleth himself with the affairs of this life”: we are not getting caught up with the Charlie Esau Kirk, whatever his name was, or the Democrats versus the Republicans. We do not care about that. “That he may please him who hath chosen him to be a soldier.” God chose you brothers to be soldiers, and our duty is to please him. How? Ecclesiastes 12:13: the whole duty of man is to keep the commandments.

“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal”. We are not going out picking up guns, and we do not want to hear of brothers doing that; our weapons are spiritual, “mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds”. Look around: all the brothers and sisters here, in the other states and around the globe, were brought into this marvellous truth not by physical warfare but by spiritual warfare, by the word of God moving them to repent.

“Casting down imaginations”: vain imaginations like you are not God’s people. We are God’s people. Stop celebrating Christmas, Thanksgiving, Easter and Halloween; our high holy days are in Leviticus 23. Everything that exalts itself above God we bring down, “bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”.

sense.text: Right now it is spiritual warfare; only when Christ comes back will it be physical warfare. This is speaking of Edom: “Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon”, “for thou shalt no more be called tender and delicate.” “Uncover thy locks, make bare the leg, uncover the thigh”, so that everybody can see your nakedness, your wickedness, because you profess yourself godly and you are not.

“Thy nakedness shall be uncovered, yea, thy shame shall be seen”. Who makes his shame seen? Us, by teaching, revealing with the Bible all the lies this man has told. That is why everybody is rising up now saying the so-called Jews are not the real Jews: they see the evil Amalek is doing, because the Israelites are rising up, and they cannot stop it.

“I will take vengeance, and I will not meet thee as a man.” The same man they hung on the cross is not coming back like that. Christ is coming back with power, in his godly form. The whole world is in a fret, holding meetings over what is in the sky: they tried to shoot the chariot with a carnal, man-made Hellfire missile, and nothing happened. They cannot stop the Most High. That is what the whole world is afraid of: a big negro coming out of the sky, and nothing they can do to stop him. No missiles, guns or drones will stop him; all of it will be turned to dust.

“For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies”: not just Esau, the so-called white man, but all nations, because all nations took part in our destruction (Psalms 83). “He hath delivered them to the slaughter”: he tells you what he is going to do before it happens.
“The heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: that is the mushroom cloud. “And all their host shall fall down”: satellites, missiles, everything.

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven”: heaven means kingdom. “It shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.” Idumea is the so-called white man. “The Lord hath a sacrifice in Bozrah, and a great slaughter in the land of Idumea”: Esau is going to be that sacrifice; he is going to be the ransom.

“For it is the day of the Lord’s vengeance, and the year of recompences for the controversy of Zion.” What is the controversy of Zion? The whole world wants to know who the Jews are, and surely it is not the so-called white man in Israel.

precepts.why:
“I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there for my people and for my heritage Israel, whom they have scattered among the nations, and parted my land.”

They scattered the nation and parted the land: you have the Israelis and the Palestinians in our land, and one group is posing as us. That is the controversy of Zion.

sense.text: The last scripture: “Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”.

“Behold, I have made thee small among the heathen: thou art greatly despised. The pride of thine heart hath deceived thee”. This is talking about Edom: Esau, your heart has deceived you. Now you have given this Charlie guy a national holiday, but where was the uproar over George Floyd, knelt on by the neck?

“Thou that dwellest in the clefts of the rock”: the cave dweller, “that saith in his heart, Who shall bring me down to the ground?”
No nation can bring this man down, but Christ is going to bring him down: “though thou set thy nest among the stars, thence will I bring thee down, saith the Lord.”
“If thieves came to thee, if robbers by night”: this man steals everything. He steals the air; he taxes rainwater.
“All the men of thy confederacy have brought thee even to the border”: his allies are going to turn on him.
“Shall I not in that day, saith the Lord, even destroy the wise men out of Edom”: Teman, the wise men, the scientists and so forth.

“For thy violence against thy brother Jacob shame shall cover thee, and thou shalt be cut off for ever.” That continual violence, that perpetual hatred, goes on to this day: two brothers were found hanged in Mississippi on the same day, still in 2025, and they say that was a long time ago.

“But upon mount Zion shall be deliverance, and there shall be holiness”: who delivers us? Christ. “And the house of Jacob shall possess their possessions”: we are going to possess them who had us in possession.

“And the house of Jacob shall be a fire, and the house of Joseph a flame, and the house of Esau for stubble”: baby stubble, grandma stubble, uncle stubble. “There shall not be any remaining of the house of Esau; for the Lord hath spoken it.” Christ is our tabernacle.
